title: Morphing Geometry Playground
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D morphing geometry playground using Three.js. Follow these exact specifications:

## Scene Setup
- Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at the origin.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Set the scene background to color 0x1a1a2e.
- Add an AmbientLight (0xffffff, 0.4) and a DirectionalLight (0xffffff, 0.8) at position (5, 10, 5).
- Add a subtle PointLight (0x00ffcc, 0.5) at position (-3, 2, -3).

## 3D Model
- Load 'DamagedHelmet.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (e.g., https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js).
- Place the loaded helmet model at the origin. Store a reference to the helmet mesh.
- The helmet should be visible initially.

## Morph Target Geometries
- Create 4 primitive geometries that serve as morph targets: Sphere (radius 1, 32 segments), Torus (radius 0.8, tube 0.3, 32, 16), Icosahedron (radius 1, detail 1), and TorusKnot (radius 0.7, tube 0.25, 64, 8).
- Create a single mesh that starts as a Sphere geometry with a MeshStandardMaterial (color 0x00ffcc, metalness 0.6, roughness 0.3, wireframe initially false).
- Position this morph mesh at (0, 0, 0). It should overlap with the helmet initially but the helmet is shown first.

## Morph Mode System
- Track a 'currentShape' index (0=Sphere, 1=Torus, 2=Icosahedron, 3=TorusKnot).
- When morphing between shapes, animate a 'morphProgress' from 0.0 to 1.0 over 1.5 seconds using lerp on vertex positions (or simply swap geometry and scale-animate from 0.01 to 1.0 over 1.5 seconds for simplicity).
- Track 'isMorphing' boolean during transitions.

## Display Modes
- Track 'displayMode': 0 = helmet visible + morph mesh hidden, 1 = helmet hidden + morph mesh visible, 2 = both visible (helmet semi-transparent at opacity 0.4).
- Press 'D' key to cycle through display modes (0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0).

## User Interactions
1. Press '1','2','3','4' keys to morph to Sphere, Torus, Icosahedron, TorusKnot respectively. Only works if not currently morphing and displayMode is not 0.
2. Press 'W' to toggle wireframe on the morph mesh material.
3. Press 'D' to cycle display mode.
4. Press 'R' to start/stop auto-rotation of the scene (rotate the parent group containing both objects around Y axis).
5. Press 'C' to cycle the morph mesh color through: 0x00ffcc, 0xff006e, 0xffd166, 0x06d6a0 (index 0-3).
6. Press 'Space' to reset everything to initial state (displayMode=0, currentShape=0, wireframe=false, rotation=false, colorIndex=0).

## HUD / UI
- Add a DOM overlay panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, padding 15px, font-family monospace) showing:
  - Current Shape: [name]
  - Display Mode: [0/1/2]
  - Wireframe: [on/off]
  - Auto-Rotate: [on/off]
  - Color: [index]
  - Morph Progress: [0.00 - 1.00]

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - helmetLoaded: boolean (true once GLTF is loaded)
  - currentShape: number (0-3)
  - currentShapeName: string ('Sphere','Torus','Icosahedron','TorusKnot')
  - displayMode: number (0-2)
  - wireframe: boolean
  - autoRotate: boolean
  - colorIndex: number (0-3)
  - morphProgress: number (0.0 to 1.0, 1.0 when morph complete)
  - isMorphing: boolean
  - helmetVisible: boolean
  - morphMeshVisible: boolean
  - rotationY: number (current Y rotation of the group in radians)
  - meshScaleX: number (scale.x of morph mesh)

## Animation Loop
- In the animation loop, if autoRotate is true, rotate the parent group by 0.01 radians per frame around Y.
- Update all __3D_STATE__ fields each frame.
- Update the HUD text each frame.
physics_constraints: Morph transitions must complete in ~1.5 seconds with smooth interpolation. Scale must remain positive and reach 1.0 when morph completes. Rotation must accumulate continuously when auto-rotate is enabled. No NaN values in any state fields.
